Playbook.name: Windows — Potential Ransomware Behavior - High count of Readme files by System - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The System process (PID 4) created a high count of ransom-note-style files (readme/lock/how-to/recover/decrypt/restore names) - the ransom-note-dropping behavior of ransomware writing over SMB. Triage question: is ransomware actively encrypting/dropping notes, or a false match on legitimate files?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Mass ransom-note creation by System (PID 4, i.e. remote SMB writes) indicates ransomware encrypting file shares - time-critical.

LogSources.LogSource: Sysmon file events + Windows Security SMB - logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Ransom-note burst
Signal.Details: PID 4 file creation of many readme/lock/recover/decrypt-named files.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host (file server) where the notes appeared.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Confirm whether ransomware is actively dropping ransom notes / encrypting, and identify the source of the SMB writes.

Step.name: Confirm the ransom-note-style file burst
Step.Purpose: Confirm the volume and naming of the created files - a real ransom-note burst has many uniform-named notes.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "11" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.pid == 4 AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | STATS files = COUNT(*), sample_names = VALUES(file.name), exts = VALUES(file.extension), dirs = COUNT_DISTINCT(file.directory) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Many identically-named readme/decrypt files across many directories = active ransomware. A handful of legitimately-named readme files is a false match. dirs count shows spread.

Step.name: Which remote source is writing over SMB
Step.Purpose: PID 4 writes come from a remote SMB client - identify it to contain the encrypting host.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "5145" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS accesses = COUNT(*), shares = VALUES(winlog.event_data.ShareName), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName) BY src | SORT accesses DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: The top SMB source writing to the shares during the note burst is the encrypting host - isolate it immediately. The account tells you which credential is compromised.

Node.Condition: INV-01 confirms many uniform ransom-note files across directories, and INV-02 identifies a remote SMB source.
Node.Result: True Positive (Active Ransomware - ISOLATE the source host NOW, activate ransomware IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows only a few legitimately-named readme files (documentation), no encryption pattern.
Ransom-note-like files present but the encrypting source cannot yet be identified.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-RANSOM-FILES, INV-02-RANSOM-SOURCE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A false match on legitimate readme/documentation files.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the files are benign; close as false_positive; tune the name patterns if needed.

TruePositive.Definition: Active ransomware dropping notes / encrypting shares.

Indicators.Item: Many uniform ransom notes across directories.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the encrypting source host and the file server immediately; activate ransomware IR.
Disable the compromised account; protect/verify backups; scope the spread.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured app mass-creating files matching the pattern.

Indicators.Item: A known app creating many readme-named files.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the app; tune the rule; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
